record.original_question: If a measure-preserving automorphism is mixing, must it satisfy light twofold mixing? Here light twofold mixing means that for every sequences m_i, n_i -> +infinity and every measurable sets A, B, C of positive measure, one has lim sup_i mu(A intersect T^{m_i}B intersect T^{m_i+n_i}C) > 0.

evidence.quote: Будем говорить, что перемешивающий автоморфизм T обладает легким перемешиванием кратности 2, если для всяких последовательностей mi, ni → +∞ и множеств A, B, C положительной меры выполнено lim sup i→∞ µ(A ∩ T^{mi}B ∩ T^{mi+ni}C) > 0.
Q5. Влечет ли перемешивание легкое перемешивание кратности 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation. Recall that $T$ is called mixing if for every measurable sets $A,B\subset X$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A\cap T^{n}B)=\mu(A)\mu(B).$$
Say that $T$ has light twofold mixing if for every pair of sequences of positive integers $m_i\to+\infty$ and $n_i\to+\infty$, and for every measurable sets $A,B,C\subset X$ of positive measure,
$$\limsup_{i\to\infty}\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{m_i}B\cap T^{m_i+n_i}C\bigr)>0.$$
Question: Does mixing of $T$ imply that $T$ has light twofold mixing?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a weakening of Rokhlin's classical multiple mixing problem (whether mixing implies twofold/threefold mixing), which remains open in general after 75+ years. Recent surveys on Rokhlin's problem (2024) discuss related variants such as light multiple mixing without indicating a resolution of this specific implication, suggesting it is open.

status_evidence.title: Multiple mixing, 75 years of Rokhlin's problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on Rokhlin's problem on multiple mixing, noting it remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of whether mixing implies higher-order mixing properties is still open.

status_evidence.title: Twofold mixing implies threefold mixing for rank one transformations
status_evidence.claim: Implications of mixing on higher-order mixing are known only in special classes such as rank-one.
